newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline drops with crude as arb creeks shut.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline drops with crude as arb creeks shut.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices ended sharply lower on Thursday after crude oil futures dropped to their weakest level since the middle of September.
The arbitrage for larger vessels, which had been open the last few weeks and was seen as a lifeline for the NWE market, was also seen as starting to shut for gasoline, traders said.
The arb already has been closed for smaller cargoes.
Some traders have cautioned that material may stay in Northwest Europe, hurting ARA barges, if the arb closed.
Eurograde barges ended $4 lower at $215/$217 fob ARA. Trades were heard at $219, at $217 for Rotterdam running refinery material, and as low as $214 and $213.
Late offers for premium unleaded cargoes were heard at $217.50 cif, down about $6.50 from Wednesday.
Industry sources said on Thursday that gasoline inventories held in independent tankage in the ARA area rose in the latest week, to 575,000-600,000 tonnes, from 550,000-575,000.
Stocks are about 75,000 tonnes or 15 percent above a year ago.
One broker said the arb was still open for other material, such as Russian, but that premium unleaded supplies may end up staying in NWE.
He minimised news on Wednesday that Poland's Gdansk refinery said it will import 500,000 tonnes of refined oil products when it shuts down its refinery for renovation from April 28 to June 22.
"There will be some buying interest...maybe at the end of February and early March," but not to the extent the refinery said it will later this spring, he said.
